title: Explicit bulk selection and scoped actions
summary: When users act on many items, make selection mode, selected count, action scope, and the path back to no selection explicit.
problem: Bulk operations become dangerous when users cannot tell which items are selected or whether an action applies to visible, filtered, or all records.
use_when: Users routinely act on multiple rows or items
avoid_when: Bulk actions are rare and add persistent complexity to every row
rationale: Selection changes the scope of actions and therefore needs its own visible state.
Danger increases when filters or pagination affect hidden selected items.

use_if: Users routinely act on multiple rows or items
prefer_alternatives_if: Single-item actions dominate and bulk selection would add persistent noise

requirements: Expose selected state and selected count programmatically.
Keep select-all semantics clear, especially across pagination or filters.
Ensure bulk action controls are keyboard reachable.
Define whether select-all means current page, current filter, or entire dataset.
Clear or preserve selection predictably after actions.
